newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-JACQUET DRAWS UP PRE-WORLD CUP LIST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JACQUET DRAWS UP PRE-WORLD CUP LIST.

text.p: France coach Aime Jacquet announced a list on Tuesday of 37 players he has in mind for next year's World Cup finals.
"The World Cup has already started," Jacquet said. "You have to do things as if we were already there.
"(The list) is a photograph of what is best at the moment in French football," added Jacquet, who named six players of league leaders Monaco.
UEFA Cup semifinalists Monaco's fine form was rewarded with first ever call-ups to the full national team for teenage striker Thierry Henry and midfielder Sylvain Legwinski.

Monaco defenders Emmanuel Petit, capped several times in the early 1990s, Patrick Blondeau and Martin Djetou, who came on for 14 minutes against Turkey in October, and goalkeeper Fabien Barthez were also included.

From the list, Jacquet will pick a reduced squad of 18 on Monday for the friendly international against Sweden at Parc des Princes next Wednesday and, nearer the date, his squad for the World Cup warm-up Tournament of France in June.
Legwinski, Nantes forward Claude Makelele, Auxerre's front men Lilian Laslandes and Bernard Diomede and France under-21 goalkeeper Lionel Letizi of Metz have never been called before.

Jacquet was tight lipped at a news conference, refusing to be drawn by questions about his choices, particularly in attack where Laslandes is included but not Strasbourg's David Zitelli, top scorer in the first division.
"You have to interpret this list with a lot of precaution, it is not closed," said Jacquet, who has also again left out English-based veterans Eric Cantona and David Ginola.
"I don't want to feel tied, nothing is ever definitive. The (team) doctor could still go abroad to examine other players. This is a revue of the troops."
Jacquet has taken advantage of the fact that there is no league football in Europe's major leagues this weekend to gather all his potential World Cup players for a spell together.
The players will undergo tests and medical check-ups and do some training together at the French team's headquarters outside Paris over the weekend.
Leaving aside the five goalkeepers, who all play their club football in France, exactly half the squad are foreign-based.
Notable absentees are Euro 96 squad members Vincent Guerin and Alain Roche of Paris St Germain, Internazionale defender Jocelyn Angloma and Deportivo Coruna's Corentin Martins.
Goalkeepers - Fabien Barthez (Monaco), Lionel Charbonnier (Auxerre), Bernard Lama (Paris St Germain), Lionel Letizi (Metz), Christophe Revault (Le Havre)

Defenders - Laurent Blanc (Barcelona), Patrick Blondeau (Monaco), Vincent Candela (AS Roma), Marcel Desailly (AC Milan), Alain Goma (Auxerre), Pierre Laigle (Sampdoria), Franck Lebouef (Chelsea), Bixente Lizarazu (Athletic Bilbao), Bruno N'Gotty (PSG), Lilian Thuram (Parma)

Midfielders - Didier Deschamps (Juventus), Martin Djetou (Monaco), Franck Gava (Lyon), Christian Karembeu (Sampdoria), Sabri Lamouchi (Auxerre), Sylvain Legwinski (Monaco), Claude Makelele (Nantes), Emmanuel Petit (Monaco), Patrick Vieira (Arsenal), Zinedine Zidane (Juventus)

Forwards - Ibrahim Ba (Bordeaux), Youri Djorkaeff (Inter Milan), Bernard Diomede (Auxerre), Christophe Dugarry (AC Milan), Thierry Henry (Monaco), Marc Keller (Karlsruhe), Lilian Laslandes (Auxerre), Patrice Loko (PSG), Florian Maurice (Lyon), Nicolas Ouedec (Espanyol), Reynald Pedros (Parma), Robert Pires (Metz).
